translations.title: Sentimental Self-Euthanasia
translations.text:
I got out of the way
so as not to be a nuisance,
so as not to cry out
any more plaintive verses.

I spent many days without writing,
without seeing you,
eating nothing but tears.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: From Everyday Life
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: In the Tree of My Chest
translations.text:
In the tree of my chest
there is a scarlet bird.
When I see you, it startles,
flutters, leaps about.

In the tree of my chest
there is a scarlet bird.
When I see you, it startles:
you are a scarecrow!
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Sailor Without Land...
translations.text:
Sailor without land,
shipwrecked man without sails,
orphan without a harbor,
ship without a helm.

Surrounded by water and thirsty,
surrounded by fish and hungry,
surrounded by waves and no greetings,
surrounded by dollars and naked.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Even If We Did Not Die When We Died
translations.text:
Even if we did not die when we died,
the word fits that passage well: Death.

Death is when those we love do not look at us;
death is being left alone, mute and still,
unable to shout that you are still alive.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: The Dictator's Statue Committed Suicide
translations.text:
The dictator's statue
committed suicide.

The statue lived in the center of the pond.
One windy night
the statue threw itself into the water.
The dictator's statue
drowned.

Only the seagulls missed it.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: In Poems...
translations.text:
In poems
I must make you do or feel what I feel,
see what I see,
hear what I hear,
love what I love.

I am strong, you know that,
but sometimes I crack
and furious, terrified verses
come out of me.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Poetry Should Not Be a Weapon...
translations.text:
Poetry should not be a weapon;
it should be an embrace,
an invention,
a way to show others
what is happening inside them:
that, a discovery,
a breath,
an addition,
a shiver.

Poetry should be
compulsory.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: People Say
translations.text:
People say:
“There will always have to be poor people,”
and they feel perfectly at ease,
so narrow in their outlook,
so empty in spirit,
so full of comfort.

I declare
with feeling
that in a coming future
only those who choose poverty will be poor.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: I Write
translations.text:
I write without a model,
whatever comes out;
I write from memory,
all at once;
I write about myself,
about people,
like a tragic game of solitaire
without cards.

I shuffle colors,
loves,
city people,
violent words,
and instead of giving myself over to hatred
or taking to the street,
I write whatever comes out.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.
